ALBERT-LUDWIGS-UNIVERSITÄT FREIBURG IM BREISGAU
(Founded 1457 — OCR rendered from Fraktur/Blackletter typeface)

[OCR NOTE: Fraktur typeface causes systematic character substitutions]
[ß→B, ü→u, ö→o, ä→a, long-s (ſ) → f or i]

ZEUGNIß
über die Promotionsprüfung

Herr Hans-Joachim von Holzhaußen
geboren zu München am 15. März 1928
hat die akademiſche Würde eines
Doktors der Naturwiſſenſchaften
erlangt nach Ablegung der vorgeſchriebenen Prüfungen
und Verteidigung ſeiner Diſſertation
"Über die Quantenmechanik des Waſſerſtoffatoms"
mit dem Urteil: ſehr gut (magna cum laude)

Freiburg im Breisgau, den 12. Juli 1955

Der Rektor: [Rektor-Siegel]
Der Dekan der Naturwiſſenſchaftlichen Fakultät: [Dekan-Siegel]
why_adversarial: This pre-war German doctoral diploma uses Fraktur (Blackletter) typeface, which Azure DI and most OCR engines handle poorly: (a) the long-s (ſ) is misread as 'f' or 'i' — 'Dissertation' becomes 'Difsertation'; (b) 'ß' becomes 'B' — 'Zeugniß' becomes 'Zeugni B'; (c) the document is from 1955 — historical German academic documents use formal Fraktur. A classifier that relies on modern keyword matching ('Zeugnis', 'Doktor') will miss the OCR-corrupted variants. The document clearly describes a doctorate (Doctor of Natural Sciences, magna cum laude, thesis defense) but the OCR output is systematically degraded. Expected: DIPLOMA at moderate confidence triggering escalation.
classifier_failure_mode: Classifier emits UNKNOWN because keywords like 'Zeugnis'/'Dissertation' are corrupted to 'Zeugni B'/'Difsertation' by Fraktur OCR. Or classifier emits ACADEMIC_TRANSCRIPT (confused by grades/scores) rather than DIPLOMA (the document confers the doctorate, it is not a grade sheet).
gold_signals_expected: ZEUGNI_ header (corrupted Zeugniß) at top of document
Doctor/Doktor degree conferral language present despite OCR corruption
University name with founding date — established academic institution
Rector/Dean seal references confirm official conferral document
notes: ISCED level 8 (doctorate) should be inferrable despite Fraktur OCR corruption. The signals array must cite the surviving readable cues — university name header, rector/dean seal references, magna cum laude grade string — NOT the corrupted Fraktur tokens directly. The 1955 date means anabin lookup will likely return 'not found' — this is expected and must not lower classification confidence.
